title: Midwives: Pharaoh kills males, spares females
english: The king [[who did not know Joseph >> Bible:Exodus 1:8]] keeps inventing new arts against God’s people. He even turns midwives — whose craft is to save life — into instruments of death: [[kill the male; keep the female alive >> Bible:Exodus 1:15-16]]. They [[feared God and kept the males alive >> Bible:Exodus 1:17]]. Friends of the letter stumble here; we learn that the law is spiritual. Woman figures flesh and its affections; man the rational sense that can [[seek the things above >> Bible:Colossians 3:1]]. Pharaoh, [[prince of this world >> Bible:John 16:11]], hates that male mind and nourishes only what is carnal. When you see people given to luxury, know he is killing males and sparing females; when you see [[one of a thousand >> Bible:Ecclesiastes 7:28]] turn toward God, know Pharaoh pursues him with a thousand devices.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.
After Homilia I tip 5b9a8a3c; Pass A ≠ Pass B.

title: Sephora and Phua: learning that fears God
english: [[The midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded >> Bible:Exodus 1:17]]. Some before us saw in them the form of rational learning — a midwife’s craft that fosters both male and female births. Sephora, interpreted “sparrow,” lifts minds on the wings of doctrine; Phua, “red” or “modest,” trains manners and honesty. Better still: the two figure both Testaments — Sephora the [[spiritual law >> Bible:Romans 7:14]], Phua the Gospels flushed with Christ’s blood. That they [[made themselves houses because they feared God >> Bible:Exodus 1:21]] makes little sense as bare letter; it fits when fear of God fills the world with houses of prayer. So fear God, refuse Egypt’s command to love the present age, and keep alive the male within — the [[inner person >> Bible:Ephesians 3:16]] healed by good acts and thoughts. [[The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom >> Bible:Psalm 111:10]].
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.
After Homilia I tip 5b9a8a3c; Pass A ≠ Pass B.

title: Hide the newborn male from the river
english: Pharaoh next bids his people seize the Hebrew infant at birth and cast him into the river. So the [[prince of this world >> Bible:John 16:11]] ambushes our beginnings — as Jesus, [[led by the Spirit into the desert to be tempted >> Bible:Matthew 4:1]], opened the path of victory by fasting and prayer. If I give alms, I beget a “male,” a work of God; but if I do it [[to be seen by people >> Bible:Matthew 6:1]], Egyptians snatch it and drown it. Hide what the right hand does; [[pray to the Father in secret >> Bible:Matthew 6:6]]. You who hear are not being told old tales, but taught the order of a living faith.

title: Moses in the basket — Homilia II CLOSEOUT
english: [[Seeing the child was beautiful, they hid him three months >> Bible:Exodus 2:2]], then set him in a bitumen-sealed basket by the river. Pharaoh’s daughter — the church gathered from the nations — comes to the waters to wash from her father’s house, [[hears “Daughter, forget your father’s house” >> Bible:Psalm 45:11]], and receives the infant with mercy. Moses names the Law: shut in cheap coverings of literal Jewish reading until the church takes him from the marsh into royal rooms. Grown strong, the veil of the letter lifts and solid food appears [[Hebrews 5:12-14 >> Bible:Hebrews 5:12-14]]. The synagogue’s “wage” is that, seeing Gentiles worship one God, she blushes to serve idols still [[Deuteronomy 32:21 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:21]]. Though Pharaoh once fathered us in evil works, when we come to the waters let us take up a great Moses — nothing small, everything spiritual — and ask Christ to reveal how great he is. [[To him be glory forever. Amen >> Bible:1 Peter 4:11]].
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.
After Homilia I tip 5b9a8a3c; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
